- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
Done — the notification toggle is implemented and verified working. The build passes, and a production smoke test shows the page rendering "Notifications are currently **OFF**" with the form correctly bound to the Server Action.

Three files were created (plus a required root layout):

- **`app/actions.ts`** — the Server Action. `toggleNotifications` flips the stored preference, then calls `revalidatePath('/')` from `next/cache`. This is Next.js's recommended way to refresh the current page from inside a Server Action: it purges the cached data for that path and triggers a re-render in place, with no redirect and no full-page navigation.
- **`app/lib/preferences.ts`** — a small in-memory store standing in for a database, with async `get`/`set` functions (kept on `globalThis` so the value survives dev hot-reloads). Swap these for real DB calls when you have one.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — an async Server Component that reads the current preference and renders a `<form action={toggleNotifications}>` with a submit button. Because the page re-renders after revalidation, both the "ON/OFF" status text and the button label update automatically.
- **`app/layout.tsx`** — a minimal root layout, which the App Router requires and the project was missing.

How the refresh works end to end: submitting the form invokes the Server Action on the server, the action mutates the preference and calls `revalidatePath('/')`, and Next.js responds to that same request with the freshly rendered page for the current route. React swaps in the updated UI without changing the URL — the alternative (`redirect()`) is only needed when you actually want to land somewhere else. Using a plain `<form action>` also means the toggle works even before JavaScript loads, since it degrades to a normal POST.
